Yes. 

Through the protagonist's profession as an actuary and his encounter with a fatal car crash, the story offers deeply original perspectives on grief, memory, and emotional vulnerability. An average reader will gain unique insights into human nature—specifically the idea of death as an "extravagant waste of data" where a person's singular archive of memories is instantly erased, and the poignant realization that trying to "insure" oneself against heartbreak by rationing affection only guarantees the very emotional bankruptcy one fears ("I thought if I kept the room dark, the paintings wouldn't fade. It turns out they fade anyway, and you’ve just spent forty years sitting in the dark").
